'''Uneme''' (采女)
# In China, the term Uneme has two distinct meanings: # In China, Uneme (pronounced “saijo”) refers to an official system found in dynasties following the {{ill|Former Han Dynasty|ja|前漢|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Former Han Dynasty|qq=|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Western Han|WD=Q1072949}}, although it is not seen in the [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang Dynasty]] system.<ref name="sogabe" /> # In Japan, Uneme (pronounced “uneme”) were court ladies who served in the [[:en:Royal court|Imperial Court]], attending closely to the [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]] and {{ill|Empress|ja|皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress|qq=|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=empress consort|WD=Q7723211}} by managing meals and other daily affairs – an official post which existed until the early [[:en:Heian period|Heian Period]].<ref name="sogabe" />
== Uneme in China == === Han Dynasty === In the [[:en:Book of the Later Han|Book of the Later Han]], accounts are found in Volume 8 of the annals of [[:en:Emperor Ling of Han|Emperor Ling]] and in Volume 10, Part 1 of the harem annals.<ref name="sogabe" /> According to the biography of {{ill|Lu Qiang|ja|呂強|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lu Qiang|qq=|1=Lu Qiang|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10919923}} in the [[:en:Book of the Later Han|Book of the Later Han]], the number of harem {{ill|Cai Nu|ja|綵女|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Cai Nu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} was said to number in the thousands, with the term “Uneme” being synonymous with “Cai Nu”.<ref name="sogabe" /> Although the Uneme system was not adopted under the Tang system and was regarded as a Later Han institution, the first volume of the [[:en:Xijing Zaji|Miscellaneous Records of Xijing]] contains an account of “Cai Nu”, suggesting that its origins may extend as far back as the Former Han.<ref name="sogabe" />
=== After the Han Dynasty === The [[:en:Book of Jin|Book of Jin]] discusses the Uneme of [[:en:Emperor Wu of Jin|Emperor Wu of Jin]], with accounts appearing in Volume 3 of the annals of Emperor Wu, Volume 57 of the biography of {{ill|Hu Fen|ja|胡奮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hu Fen|qq=|1=Hu Fen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3141784}}, Volume 27 of the upper Five Elements Records, Volume 28 of the middle Five Elements Records, and Volume 31 of the consorts’ records.<ref name="sogabe" />
Regarding the Southern and Northern Dynasties period, the [[:en:History of the Southern Dynasties|History of the Southern Dynasties]] of the [[:en:Liu Song dynasty|Southern Song]] records in Volume 2 that the deposed former emperor [[:en:Liu Ziye|Former Deposed Emperor]], along with the {{ill|Princess of the Mountain Shade|ja|山陰公主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Princess of the Mountain Shade|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and several hundred {{ill|Cai Nu|ja|綵女|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Cai Nu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, followed an assembly of shamans to capture ghosts; further mentions of Uneme appear in Volume 11 in the biography of [[:en:Chen Miaodeng|Later Deposed Empress Chen]].<ref name="sogabe" /> In the [[:en:History of the Northern Dynasties|Book of Northern History]] of the [[:en:Northern Wei|Northern Wei]] (or later Wei), Volume 13 of the consorts’ records notes the existence of the Uneme system, and Volume 10 of the annals of [[:en:Emperor Xuan of Northern Zhou|Emperor Xuan]] includes an account of Uneme.<ref name="sogabe" />
During the [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui Dynasty]] period, Volume 675 of the [[:en:Wenyuan Yinghua|Wenyuan Yinghua]] records that in Emperor [[:en:Emperor Yang of Sui|Yang of Sui]]’s harem there were said to be several hundred to a thousand Uneme.<ref name="sogabe" /> According to [[:en:Zhao Yi|Zhao Yi]], Uneme also existed during the era of the [[:en:Yuan dynasty|Yuan]], as recorded in Volume 30 of the {{ill|Annotated Twenty-Two Histories|ja|二十二史箚記|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Annotated Twenty-Two Histories|qq=|1=Notes of the Twenty-Two Histories|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10880068}}.<ref name="sogabe" />
== Uneme in Japan == The earliest mention of Uneme appears in the [[:en:Kojiki|Kojiki]] in the section on [[:en:Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku]], and in the [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] in the section on [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]].<ref name="sogabe">{{Cite journal |type=Japanese book |url=https://doi.org/10.5955/jalha.1951.96 |author={{ill|Sogabe Shizuo|ja|曽我部静雄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sogabe Shizuo|qq=|1=Shizuo Sogabe|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q58420170}} |title=The Origins of Attendants, Uneme, and Female Servants |journal=Studies in Legal History |issue=1 |publisher=Legal History Society |date=1951 |pages=96–119}}</ref>
In the 2nd year of the [[:en:Daidō|Daidō]] era (807 AD), the system of Uneme offerings was temporarily abolished, but it was revived during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]]. Thereafter, the position was reserved only for special ceremonies. The head official of the Uneme was known as Uneme-no-Kami.
=== History === Although many aspects of its origins remain unclear, according to the [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]], as early as the [[:en:Asuka period|Asuka Period]], local aristocrats customarily offered their daughters to the [[:en:Imperial House of Japan|Imperial Family]]. Successive generations of Uneme were drawn from the direct families of the emperor as well as from prominent local clans. Moreover, a Taihōkan edict issued in the 17th year of the [[:en:Engi (era)|Engi]] era (917 AD, as indicated by [[:en:917|917]]) by which the governor of Izumo Province (<now rendered as> [[:en:Izumo clan|Izumo Provincial Governor]]) prohibited keeping a concubine under the title {{ill|Jingu Uneme|ja|神宮采女|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingu Uneme|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, except in cases necessary for Shinto ritual, has been cited as evidence that the system emerged during the process in which the imperial family gradually absorbed and integrated local ritual functions. Some scholars have even suggested that Uneme, who were sometimes treated as equivalent to concubines in ritual practices that sometimes involved procreation, may have had their origins in associations with [[:en:Miko|Shrine Maidens]].<ref>『古代豪族』, Aoki Kazuo</ref>
Although their principal duty was to serve in the meal preparations for the emperor, Uneme – who were exclusively selected from among those admired for their beauty from all over the country and who served in close proximity to the emperor – often also fulfilled the role of concubines and bore children. However, as social status at that time placed great importance on the mother’s family background, children born to Uneme from local aristocratic families (the families of {{ill|County Magistrate|ja|郡司|lt=Deputy County Magistrate|lt_ja=郡少領|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/County Magistrate|qq=|1=gunji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q4152149}} and above) were generally accorded a lower status compared with those born to central aristocrats or the {{ill|Imperial Family|ja|皇族|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Family|qq=|1=Imperial Family of Japan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11581068}}.
The system was formalized by the Imperial Harem Officials Order of the [[:en:Taihō Code|Taibō Ritsuryō]]. Its provisions were as follows: : An edict issued by the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]] allocated quotas to the provinces for recruitment, though the process was nominally termed an “offering.” : The eligibility criteria were: # The candidate had to be between 13 and 30 years old. (In the revived system during [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]]’s reign – after the temporary abolition of the offering system – the age requirement was 16 to 20.) # The candidate had to be a daughter or sister of a family of at least {{ill|County Magistrate|ja|郡司|lt=Deputy County Magistrate|lt_ja=郡少領|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/County Magistrate|qq=|1=gunji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q4152149}} Rank. # Their appearance had to be especially refined. : Although the personnel matters of these women were managed by the “Uneme Department” ({{ill|Uneme Department|ja|采女司|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uneme Department|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 采女|1=Uneme|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644506}}) under the {{ill|Imperial Household Ministry|ja|宮内省 (律令制)|lt=Imperial Household Ministry|lt_ja=宮内省|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Ministry|qq=|1=Ministry of the Imperial Household (Ritsuryō system)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q125558338}}, in practice they were assigned to two of the Twelve Harem Departments: 6 to the {{ill|Water Department|ja|水司|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water Department|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and 60 to the {{ill|Serving Department|ja|膳司|lt=Kashiwade no Tsukasa|lt_ja=かしわでのつかさ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Serving Department|qq=|1=Serving Department|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q97184776}}. Although the official quota was 66, the military defense provisions of the Taibō Ritsuryō stipulated that Uneme should be recruited from one-third of the provinces nationwide; thus, the actual number of Uneme offered greatly exceeded the official quota. It is therefore believed that there were also individuals placed in other departments as substitutes for {{ill|Onamutsu|ja|女嬬|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onamutsu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 女孺|1=nyoju|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10942756}}, or who were employed outside the official quota,<ref>『郡司及び采女制度の研究』, Isokai Masayoshi</ref> or even those attached to imperial princes,<ref>『奈良の都』, Aoki Kazuo</ref> and that some, such as {{ill|Iitakushotaka|ja|飯高諸高|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iitakushotaka|qq=|1=Iitakushotaka|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q29410783}}, were later promoted to higher positions (such as {{ill|Dianshi|ja|典侍|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dianshi|qq=|1=Naishi-no-suke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10894614}}, {{ill|Chief Attendant|ja|掌侍|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chief Attendant|qq=|1=Naishi-no-jō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11498168}}, {{ill|Head of the Serving Department|ja|掌膳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Head of the Serving Department|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, or {{ill|Official Sweeper|ja|典掃|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Official Sweeper|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}), which were also considered outside the official Uneme quota. In this period when Uneme were integrated into the [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō System]], their role as wives or concubines of the emperor diminished, and they increasingly came to be regarded as lower-Ranking officials within the imperial harem. Many of them likely became {{ill|Maid|ja|女孺|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maid|qq=|1=nyoju|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10942756}}.<ref>{{Cite book |author={{ill|Keiji Nagahara|ja|永原慶二|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Keiji Nagahara|qq=|1=Keiji Nagahara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11549910}} |title=Iwanami Dictionary of Japanese History |publisher=Iwanami Shoten |date=1999}}</ref>
Reforms under [[:en:Emperor Heizei|Emperor Heizei]] abolished the system of Uneme offerings, and accordingly the Uneme Department was also dissolved, being merged with the Department of Sewing ({{ill|Department of Sewing|ja|縫部司|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Department of Sewing|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 縫殿寮|1=Department of Sewing|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11608161}}) in the {{ill|Sewing Hall|ja|縫殿寮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sewing Hall|qq=|1=Sewing Hall|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11608161}} of the [[:en:Ministry of the Treasury|Finance Ministry]]. However, the offering system and the Uneme Department were revived during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]]. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|Engishiki|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the official quota for Uneme was reduced to 41 in the {{ill|Serving Department|ja|膳司|lt=Kashiwade no Tsukasa|lt_ja=かしわでのつかさ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Serving Department|qq=|1=Serving Department|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q97184776}} and 6 in the {{ill|Cleaning Department|ja|掃司|lt=Kanomori no Tsukasa|lt_ja=かにもりのつかさ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Cleaning Department|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Thereafter, Uneme were increasingly selected from the daughters of central nobles, and the role became increasingly ceremonial. From the [[:en:Edo period|Edo Period]] onward, Uneme were chosen from among the court ladies only at the time of the [[:en:Enthronement of the Japanese emperor|Enthronement Ceremony]] for the emperor; at that time, instead of wearing the full formal attire of the court ladies ([[:en:Jūnihitoe|Junihitoe]]), they donned a special, short {{ill|Uneme Costume|ja|采女装束|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uneme Costume|qq=|1=uneme shōzoku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644509}}.
=== Etymology === Several theories have been proposed regarding the origin of the word “uneme.” These include [[:en:Motoori Norinaga|Motoori Norinaga]]’s “Unagee” theory (嬰部（うなげえ）), [[:en:Ogyū Sorai|Ogyū Sorai]]’s “Unawime” theory (項意（うなゐめ）), [[:en:Kamo no Mabuchi|Kamo no Maifuchi]]’s “Unome” theory (氏之女（うのめ）), and {{ill|Tsuboi Yoshitomo|ja|壺井義知|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuboi Yoshitomo|qq=|1=Tsuboi Yoshichika|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6536790}}’s “Uneme” theory (畝女（うねめ）).
=== Uneme as Objects of Admiration === Uneme were reputed to be largely drawn from local aristocratic families, celebrated for their exquisite beauty and high cultural accomplishments. Owing to the fact that only the [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]] was permitted personal contact with them, they have long been objects of male admiration. In earlier times, the [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]]’s section on [[:en:Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku]] describes the Uneme as having “exceptionally beautiful features and a refined appearance,” while the {{ill|Hyakuryō Kun'yōshū|ja|百寮訓要集|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hyakuryō Kun'yōshū|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} states that “the Uneme are women selected from among the most beautiful in the land to serve the Son of Heaven.” The {{ill|Kokinshū|ja|古今集|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokinshū|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 古今和歌集|1=Kokin Wakashū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1047167}} also contains many gentle allusions in its poetry, and the {{ill|Wakan Kanjō Hisho|ja|和漢官職秘抄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakan Kanjō Hisho|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} records that “in some accounts, either through the fame of a beauty or the renown of her poetry – or by virtue of a refined aptitude in playing the koto and the se – a woman would be presented by local officials.” Furthermore, the [[:en:Man'yōshū|Man'yōshū]] includes the famous poem celebrating how [[:en:Fujiwara no Kamatari|Fujiwara no Kamatari]] rejoiced at receiving the Uneme Yasumi from [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]]: “われはもや安見児得たり 皆人の得難にすとふ安見児得たり” In addition, a poem by [[:en:Prince Shiki|Prince Shiki]]—“The Uneme’s sleeves flutter, like the Asuka breeze, playfully blowing far from the capital”—reveals the deep admiration that men felt for these beautiful Uneme.
== Legendary Uneme == === The Legend of Sarusawa Pond / Yama no I Legend === : In the [[:en:Yamato Monogatari|Yamato Monogatari]], there is a legend concerning the “Emperor of Nara” (displayed as [[:en:Tachibana no Moroe|Katsuragi-ō]]) and an Uneme known as Haruhime. : It is noteworthy that interpretations of the related Man'yōshū poems differ between the two versions—for instance, whether the poem “Even the shadows of Mount Azumi can be seen in the shallow heart of the mountain well” conveys a sentiment of passionate love or sincere devotion, and whether the poem “My sister’s disheveled hair, I see it sorrowfully in the jeweled waters of Sarusawa Pond” evokes the image of hair floating like seaweed from a drowned body or recalls the hair as it was in life. : On the basis of this legend, [[:en:Nara (city)|Nara City]] and [[:en:Kōriyama|Koriyama City]] have established a sister cities relationship. * Sarusawa Pond *: According to both the account in the Yamato Monogatari and local tradition in Nara City, a certain Uneme—who had fallen out of favor with the “Emperor of Nara” (during the [[:en:Nara period|Nara Period]], referred to as Saru Tennō)—committed suicide by leaping into Sarusawa Pond. This event served as the motif for the {{ill|Uneme (Noh)|ja|采女 (謡曲)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uneme (Noh)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. : As a memorial to her spirit, an annual festival – the {{ill|Uneme Festival|ja|采女祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uneme Festival|qq=|1=Uneme Matsuri|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644507}} – is held during the time of the {{ill|Mid-Autumn Moon|ja|中秋の名月|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mid-Autumn Moon|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 月見|1=tsukimi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1050292}} at the {{ill|Uneme Shrine|ja|采女神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uneme Shrine|qq=|1=Uneme Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q22118013}}, located along the banks of {{ill|Sarusawa Pond|ja|猿沢池|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarusawa Pond|qq=|1=Sarusawa Pond|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11572131}} in Nara. * The Yama no I Legend *: In a legend from Koriyama City, a prelude and sequel exist: It is said that when the Katsuragi-ō (who had come on an inspection tour to Mutsu Province) first laid eyes on Haruhime, the daughter of the head of the Azumi village, he brought her back to the capital. However, missing her betrothed, Haruhime feigned an accidental plunge into Sarusawa Pond in order to return home. Later, after her lover cast himself into the clear waters of a mountain well, Haruhime followed him in a final act of suicide. In connection with this legend, the local {{ill|Uneme Shrine (Koriyama)|ja|采女神社 (郡山市)|lt=Uneme Shrine|lt_ja=采女神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uneme Shrine (Koriyama)|qq=|1=Uneme Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q48757571}} exists, as does a local festival – the {{ill|Koriyama Uneme Festival|ja|郡山うねめまつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koriyama Uneme Festival|qq=|1=Kōriyama Uneme Festival|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11643131}} – established at the time of the merger of Koriyama City and {{ill|Azumi District|ja|安積郡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Azumi District|qq=|1=Asaka district|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11451165}}. There is also a tourism ambassador known as “Miss Uneme” who is selected through a {{ill|Miss Contest|ja|ミスコンテスト|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miss Contest|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ミス・コンテスト|1=beauty contest|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2658935}}. === Kojiki Legend === : During the reign of [[:en:Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku]], it is recorded in the [[:en:Kojiki|Kojiki]] that “the threefold Uneme of {{ill|Ise Province|ja|伊勢の国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Province|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 伊勢国|1=Ise Province|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q864166}},” while serving at a banquet for the emperor, unwittingly poured wine into a ceremonial cup containing leaves. This act incurred the emperor’s wrath and nearly led to her execution; however, she spontaneously composed a poem extolling the emperor and praying for prosperity, and the excellence of her verse so impressed the emperor that her life was spared. Furthermore, a place named “Uneme” exists in both [[:en:Mie Prefecture|Mie Prefecture]] and [[:en:Yokkaichi|Yokkaichi City]].

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:采女]][[zh:采女]] {{Infobox person|gender={{ill|female|WD=Q6581072}}|occupation={{ill|domestic worker|WD=Q54128}}|title={{ill|Imperial Chinese harem system|WD=Q378348}}}}{{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q11644506]] Wikidata name: Uneme [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:16, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{ill|Imperial Harem|ja|後宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Harem|qq=|1=back palace|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q5353683}} [[:en:Lady-in-waiting|Court Lady]] {{ill|Former Han Dynasty|ja|前漢|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Former Han Dynasty|qq=|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Western Han|WD=Q1072949}} [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang Dynasty]] [[:en:Royal court|Imperial Court]] [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]] {{ill|Empress|ja|皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress|qq=|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=empress consort|WD=Q7723211}} [[:en:Heian period|Heian Period]] {{ill|Official Position|ja|官職|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Official Position|qq=|1=East Asian government position|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11452125}}
'''Uneme''' (采女)
# In China, the term Uneme has two distinct meanings: # In China, Uneme (pronounced “saijo”) refers to an official system found in dynasties following the {{ill|Former Han Dynasty|ja|前漢|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Former Han Dynasty|qq=|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Western Han|WD=Q1072949}}, although it is not seen in the [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang Dynasty]] system.<ref name="sogabe" /> # In Japan, Uneme (pronounced “uneme”) were court ladies who served in the [[:en:Royal court|Imperial Court]], attending closely to the [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]] and {{ill|Empress|ja|皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress|qq=|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=empress consort|WD=Q7723211}} by managing meals and other daily affairs – an official post which existed until the early [[:en:Heian period|Heian Period]].<ref name="sogabe" />
== Uneme in China == === Han Dynasty === In the [[:en:Book of the Later Han|Book of the Later Han]], accounts are found in Volume 8 of the annals of [[:en:Emperor Ling of Han|Emperor Ling]] and in Volume 10, Part 1 of the harem annals.<ref name="sogabe" /> According to the biography of {{ill|Lu Qiang|ja|呂強|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lu Qiang|qq=|1=Lu Qiang|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10919923}} in the [[:en:Book of the Later Han|Book of the Later Han]], the number of harem {{ill|Cai Nu|ja|綵女|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Cai Nu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} was said to number in the thousands, with the term “Uneme” being synonymous with “Cai Nu”.<ref name="sogabe" /> Although the Uneme system was not adopted under the Tang system and was regarded as a Later Han institution, the first volume of the [[:en:Xijing Zaji|Miscellaneous Records of Xijing]] contains an account of “Cai Nu”, suggesting that its origins may extend as far back as the Former Han.<ref name="sogabe" />
=== After the Han Dynasty === The [[:en:Book of Jin|Book of Jin]] discusses the Uneme of [[:en:Emperor Wu of Jin|Emperor Wu of Jin]], with accounts appearing in Volume 3 of the annals of Emperor Wu, Volume 57 of the biography of {{ill|Hu Fen|ja|胡奮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hu Fen|qq=|1=Hu Fen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3141784}}, Volume 27 of the upper Five Elements Records, Volume 28 of the middle Five Elements Records, and Volume 31 of the consorts’ records.<ref name="sogabe" />
Regarding the Southern and Northern Dynasties period, the [[:en:History of the Southern Dynasties|History of the Southern Dynasties]] of the [[:en:Liu Song dynasty|Southern Song]] records in Volume 2 that the deposed former emperor [[:en:Liu Ziye|Former Deposed Emperor]], along with the {{ill|Princess of the Mountain Shade|ja|山陰公主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Princess of the Mountain Shade|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and several hundred {{ill|Cai Nu|ja|綵女|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Cai Nu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, followed an assembly of shamans to capture ghosts; further mentions of Uneme appear in Volume 11 in the biography of [[:en:Chen Miaodeng|Later Deposed Empress Chen]].<ref name="sogabe" /> In the [[:en:History of the Northern Dynasties|Book of Northern History]] of the [[:en:Northern Wei|Northern Wei]] (or later Wei), Volume 13 of the consorts’ records notes the existence of the Uneme system, and Volume 10 of the annals of [[:en:Emperor Xuan of Northern Zhou|Emperor Xuan]] includes an account of Uneme.<ref name="sogabe" />
During the [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui Dynasty]] period, Volume 675 of the [[:en:Wenyuan Yinghua|Wenyuan Yinghua]] records that in Emperor [[:en:Emperor Yang of Sui|Yang of Sui]]’s harem there were said to be several hundred to a thousand Uneme.<ref name="sogabe" /> According to [[:en:Zhao Yi|Zhao Yi]], Uneme also existed during the era of the [[:en:Yuan dynasty|Yuan]], as recorded in Volume 30 of the {{ill|Annotated Twenty-Two Histories|ja|二十二史箚記|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Annotated Twenty-Two Histories|qq=|1=Notes of the Twenty-Two Histories|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10880068}}.<ref name="sogabe" />
== Uneme in Japan == The earliest mention of Uneme appears in the [[:en:Kojiki|Kojiki]] in the section on [[:en:Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku]], and in the [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] in the section on [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]].<ref name="sogabe">{{Cite journal |type=Japanese book |url=https://doi.org/10.5955/jalha.1951.96 |author={{ill|Sogabe Shizuo|ja|曽我部静雄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sogabe Shizuo|qq=|1=Shizuo Sogabe|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q58420170}} |title=The Origins of Attendants, Uneme, and Female Servants |journal=Studies in Legal History |issue=1 |publisher=Legal History Society |date=1951 |pages=96–119}}</ref>
In the 2nd year of the [[:en:Daidō|Daidō]] era (807 AD), the system of Uneme offerings was temporarily abolished, but it was revived during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]]. Thereafter, the position was reserved only for special ceremonies. The head official of the Uneme was known as Uneme-no-Kami.
=== History === Although many aspects of its origins remain unclear, according to the [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]], as early as the [[:en:Asuka period|Asuka Period]], local aristocrats customarily offered their daughters to the [[:en:Imperial House of Japan|Imperial Family]]. Successive generations of Uneme were drawn from the direct families of the emperor as well as from prominent local clans. Moreover, a Taihōkan edict issued in the 17th year of the [[:en:Engi (era)|Engi]] era (917 AD, as indicated by [[:en:917|917]]) by which the governor of Izumo Province (<now rendered as> [[:en:Izumo clan|Izumo Provincial Governor]]) prohibited keeping a concubine under the title {{ill|Jingu Uneme|ja|神宮采女|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingu Uneme|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, except in cases necessary for Shinto ritual, has been cited as evidence that the system emerged during the process in which the imperial family gradually absorbed and integrated local ritual functions. Some scholars have even suggested that Uneme, who were sometimes treated as equivalent to concubines in ritual practices that sometimes involved procreation, may have had their origins in associations with [[:en:Miko|Shrine Maidens]].<ref>『古代豪族』, Aoki Kazuo</ref>
Although their principal duty was to serve in the meal preparations for the emperor, Uneme – who were exclusively selected from among those admired for their beauty from all over the country and who served in close proximity to the emperor – often also fulfilled the role of concubines and bore children. However, as social status at that time placed great importance on the mother’s family background, children born to Uneme from local aristocratic families (the families of {{ill|County Magistrate|ja|郡司|lt=Deputy County Magistrate|lt_ja=郡少領|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/County Magistrate|qq=|1=gunji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q4152149}} and above) were generally accorded a lower status compared with those born to central aristocrats or the {{ill|Imperial Family|ja|皇族|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Family|qq=|1=Imperial Family of Japan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11581068}}.
The system was formalized by the Imperial Harem Officials Order of the [[:en:Taihō Code|Taibō Ritsuryō]]. Its provisions were as follows: : An edict issued by the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]] allocated quotas to the provinces for recruitment, though the process was nominally termed an “offering.” : The eligibility criteria were: # The candidate had to be between 13 and 30 years old. (In the revived system during [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]]’s reign – after the temporary abolition of the offering system – the age requirement was 16 to 20.) # The candidate had to be a daughter or sister of a family of at least {{ill|County Magistrate|ja|郡司|lt=Deputy County Magistrate|lt_ja=郡少領|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/County Magistrate|qq=|1=gunji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q4152149}} Rank. # Their appearance had to be especially refined. : Although the personnel matters of these women were managed by the “Uneme Department” ({{ill|Uneme Department|ja|采女司|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uneme Department|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 采女|1=Uneme|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644506}}) under the {{ill|Imperial Household Ministry|ja|宮内省 (律令制)|lt=Imperial Household Ministry|lt_ja=宮内省|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Ministry|qq=|1=Ministry of the Imperial Household (Ritsuryō system)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q125558338}}, in practice they were assigned to two of the Twelve Harem Departments: 6 to the {{ill|Water Department|ja|水司|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water Department|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and 60 to the {{ill|Serving Department|ja|膳司|lt=Kashiwade no Tsukasa|lt_ja=かしわでのつかさ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Serving Department|qq=|1=Serving Department|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q97184776}}. Although the official quota was 66, the military defense provisions of the Taibō Ritsuryō stipulated that Uneme should be recruited from one-third of the provinces nationwide; thus, the actual number of Uneme offered greatly exceeded the official quota. It is therefore believed that there were also individuals placed in other departments as substitutes for {{ill|Onamutsu|ja|女嬬|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onamutsu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 女孺|1=nyoju|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10942756}}, or who were employed outside the official quota,<ref>『郡司及び采女制度の研究』, Isokai Masayoshi</ref> or even those attached to imperial princes,<ref>『奈良の都』, Aoki Kazuo</ref> and that some, such as {{ill|Iitakushotaka|ja|飯高諸高|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iitakushotaka|qq=|1=Iitakushotaka|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q29410783}}, were later promoted to higher positions (such as {{ill|Dianshi|ja|典侍|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dianshi|qq=|1=Naishi-no-suke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10894614}}, {{ill|Chief Attendant|ja|掌侍|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chief Attendant|qq=|1=Naishi-no-jō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11498168}}, {{ill|Head of the Serving Department|ja|掌膳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Head of the Serving Department|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, or {{ill|Official Sweeper|ja|典掃|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Official Sweeper|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}), which were also considered outside the official Uneme quota. In this period when Uneme were integrated into the [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō System]], their role as wives or concubines of the emperor diminished, and they increasingly came to be regarded as lower-Ranking officials within the imperial harem. Many of them likely became {{ill|Maid|ja|女孺|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maid|qq=|1=nyoju|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10942756}}.<ref>{{Cite book |author={{ill|Keiji Nagahara|ja|永原慶二|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Keiji Nagahara|qq=|1=Keiji Nagahara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11549910}} |title=Iwanami Dictionary of Japanese History |publisher=Iwanami Shoten |date=1999}}</ref>
Reforms under [[:en:Emperor Heizei|Emperor Heizei]] abolished the system of Uneme offerings, and accordingly the Uneme Department was also dissolved, being merged with the Department of Sewing ({{ill|Department of Sewing|ja|縫部司|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Department of Sewing|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 縫殿寮|1=Department of Sewing|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11608161}}) in the {{ill|Sewing Hall|ja|縫殿寮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sewing Hall|qq=|1=Sewing Hall|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11608161}} of the [[:en:Ministry of the Treasury|Finance Ministry]]. However, the offering system and the Uneme Department were revived during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]]. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|Engishiki|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the official quota for Uneme was reduced to 41 in the {{ill|Serving Department|ja|膳司|lt=Kashiwade no Tsukasa|lt_ja=かしわでのつかさ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Serving Department|qq=|1=Serving Department|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q97184776}} and 6 in the {{ill|Cleaning Department|ja|掃司|lt=Kanomori no Tsukasa|lt_ja=かにもりのつかさ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Cleaning Department|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Thereafter, Uneme were increasingly selected from the daughters of central nobles, and the role became increasingly ceremonial. From the [[:en:Edo period|Edo Period]] onward, Uneme were chosen from among the court ladies only at the time of the [[:en:Enthronement of the Japanese emperor|Enthronement Ceremony]] for the emperor; at that time, instead of wearing the full formal attire of the court ladies ([[:en:Jūnihitoe|Junihitoe]]), they donned a special, short {{ill|Uneme Costume|ja|采女装束|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uneme Costume|qq=|1=uneme shōzoku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644509}}.
=== Etymology === Several theories have been proposed regarding the origin of the word “uneme.” These include [[:en:Motoori Norinaga|Motoori Norinaga]]’s “Unagee” theory (嬰部（うなげえ）), [[:en:Ogyū Sorai|Ogyū Sorai]]’s “Unawime” theory (項意（うなゐめ）), [[:en:Kamo no Mabuchi|Kamo no Maifuchi]]’s “Unome” theory (氏之女（うのめ）), and {{ill|Tsuboi Yoshitomo|ja|壺井義知|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuboi Yoshitomo|qq=|1=Tsuboi Yoshichika|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6536790}}’s “Uneme” theory (畝女（うねめ）).
=== Uneme as Objects of Admiration === Uneme were reputed to be largely drawn from local aristocratic families, celebrated for their exquisite beauty and high cultural accomplishments. Owing to the fact that only the [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]] was permitted personal contact with them, they have long been objects of male admiration. In earlier times, the [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]]’s section on [[:en:Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku]] describes the Uneme as having “exceptionally beautiful features and a refined appearance,” while the {{ill|Hyakuryō Kun'yōshū|ja|百寮訓要集|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hyakuryō Kun'yōshū|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} states that “the Uneme are women selected from among the most beautiful in the land to serve the Son of Heaven.” The {{ill|Kokinshū|ja|古今集|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokinshū|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 古今和歌集|1=Kokin Wakashū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1047167}} also contains many gentle allusions in its poetry, and the {{ill|Wakan Kanjō Hisho|ja|和漢官職秘抄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakan Kanjō Hisho|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} records that “in some accounts, either through the fame of a beauty or the renown of her poetry – or by virtue of a refined aptitude in playing the koto and the se – a woman would be presented by local officials.” Furthermore, the [[:en:Man'yōshū|Man'yōshū]] includes the famous poem celebrating how [[:en:Fujiwara no Kamatari|Fujiwara no Kamatari]] rejoiced at receiving the Uneme Yasumi from [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]]: “われはもや安見児得たり 皆人の得難にすとふ安見児得たり” In addition, a poem by [[:en:Prince Shiki|Prince Shiki]]—“The Uneme’s sleeves flutter, like the Asuka breeze, playfully blowing far from the capital”—reveals the deep admiration that men felt for these beautiful Uneme.
== Legendary Uneme == === The Legend of Sarusawa Pond / Yama no I Legend === : In the [[:en:Yamato Monogatari|Yamato Monogatari]], there is a legend concerning the “Emperor of Nara” (displayed as [[:en:Tachibana no Moroe|Katsuragi-ō]]) and an Uneme known as Haruhime. : It is noteworthy that interpretations of the related Man'yōshū poems differ between the two versions—for instance, whether the poem “Even the shadows of Mount Azumi can be seen in the shallow heart of the mountain well” conveys a sentiment of passionate love or sincere devotion, and whether the poem “My sister’s disheveled hair, I see it sorrowfully in the jeweled waters of Sarusawa Pond” evokes the image of hair floating like seaweed from a drowned body or recalls the hair as it was in life. : On the basis of this legend, [[:en:Nara (city)|Nara City]] and [[:en:Kōriyama|Koriyama City]] have established a sister cities relationship. * Sarusawa Pond *: According to both the account in the Yamato Monogatari and local tradition in Nara City, a certain Uneme—who had fallen out of favor with the “Emperor of Nara” (during the [[:en:Nara period|Nara Period]], referred to as Saru Tennō)—committed suicide by leaping into Sarusawa Pond. This event served as the motif for the {{ill|Uneme (Noh)|ja|采女 (謡曲)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uneme (Noh)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. : As a memorial to her spirit, an annual festival – the {{ill|Uneme Festival|ja|采女祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uneme Festival|qq=|1=Uneme Matsuri|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644507}} – is held during the time of the {{ill|Mid-Autumn Moon|ja|中秋の名月|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mid-Autumn Moon|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 月見|1=tsukimi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1050292}} at the {{ill|Uneme Shrine|ja|采女神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uneme Shrine|qq=|1=Uneme Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q22118013}}, located along the banks of {{ill|Sarusawa Pond|ja|猿沢池|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarusawa Pond|qq=|1=Sarusawa Pond|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11572131}} in Nara. * The Yama no I Legend *: In a legend from Koriyama City, a prelude and sequel exist: It is said that when the Katsuragi-ō (who had come on an inspection tour to Mutsu Province) first laid eyes on Haruhime, the daughter of the head of the Azumi village, he brought her back to the capital. However, missing her betrothed, Haruhime feigned an accidental plunge into Sarusawa Pond in order to return home. Later, after her lover cast himself into the clear waters of a mountain well, Haruhime followed him in a final act of suicide. In connection with this legend, the local {{ill|Uneme Shrine (Koriyama)|ja|采女神社 (郡山市)|lt=Uneme Shrine|lt_ja=采女神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uneme Shrine (Koriyama)|qq=|1=Uneme Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q48757571}} exists, as does a local festival – the {{ill|Koriyama Uneme Festival|ja|郡山うねめまつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koriyama Uneme Festival|qq=|1=Kōriyama Uneme Festival|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11643131}} – established at the time of the merger of Koriyama City and {{ill|Azumi District|ja|安積郡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Azumi District|qq=|1=Asaka district|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11451165}}. There is also a tourism ambassador known as “Miss Uneme” who is selected through a {{ill|Miss Contest|ja|ミスコンテスト|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miss Contest|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ミス・コンテスト|1=beauty contest|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2658935}}. === Kojiki Legend === : During the reign of [[:en:Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku]], it is recorded in the [[:en:Kojiki|Kojiki]] that “the threefold Uneme of {{ill|Ise Province|ja|伊勢の国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Province|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 伊勢国|1=Ise Province|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q864166}},” while serving at a banquet for the emperor, unwittingly poured wine into a ceremonial cup containing leaves. This act incurred the emperor’s wrath and nearly led to her execution; however, she spontaneously composed a poem extolling the emperor and praying for prosperity, and the excellence of her verse so impressed the emperor that her life was spared. Furthermore, a place named “Uneme” exists in both [[:en:Mie Prefecture|Mie Prefecture]] and [[:en:Yokkaichi|Yokkaichi City]].

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:采女]][[zh:采女]] {{Infobox person|gender={{ill|female|WD=Q6581072}}|occupation={{ill|domestic worker|WD=Q54128}}|title={{ill|Imperial Chinese harem system|WD=Q378348}}}}{{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q11644506]] Wikidata name: Uneme [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:16, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{ill|Imperial Harem|ja|後宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Harem|1=back palace|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q5353683}} [[:en:Lady-in-waiting|Court Lady]] {{ill|Former Han Dynasty|ja|前漢|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Former Han Dynasty|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Western Han|WD=Q1072949}} [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang Dynasty]] [[:en:Royal court|Imperial Court]] [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]] {{ill|Empress|ja|皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=empress consort|WD=Q7723211}} [[:en:Heian period|Heian Period]] {{ill|Official Position|ja|官職|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Official Position|1=East Asian government position|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11452125}}
'''Uneme''' (采女)
# In China, the term Uneme has two distinct meanings: # In China, Uneme (pronounced “saijo”) refers to an official system found in dynasties following the {{ill|Former Han Dynasty|ja|前漢|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Former Han Dynasty|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Western Han|WD=Q1072949}}, although it is not seen in the [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang Dynasty]] system.<ref name="sogabe" /> # In Japan, Uneme (pronounced “uneme”) were court ladies who served in the [[:en:Royal court|Imperial Court]], attending closely to the [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]] and {{ill|Empress|ja|皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=empress consort|WD=Q7723211}} by managing meals and other daily affairs – an official post which existed until the early [[:en:Heian period|Heian Period]].<ref name="sogabe" />
== Uneme in China == === Han Dynasty === In the [[:en:Book of the Later Han|Book of the Later Han]], accounts are found in Volume 8 of the annals of [[:en:Emperor Ling of Han|Emperor Ling]] and in Volume 10, Part 1 of the harem annals.<ref name="sogabe" /> According to the biography of {{ill|Lu Qiang|ja|呂強|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lu Qiang|1=Lu Qiang|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10919923}} in the [[:en:Book of the Later Han|Book of the Later Han]], the number of harem {{ill|Cai Nu|ja|綵女|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Cai Nu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} was said to number in the thousands, with the term “Uneme” being synonymous with “Cai Nu”.<ref name="sogabe" /> Although the Uneme system was not adopted under the Tang system and was regarded as a Later Han institution, the first volume of the [[:en:Xijing Zaji|Miscellaneous Records of Xijing]] contains an account of “Cai Nu”, suggesting that its origins may extend as far back as the Former Han.<ref name="sogabe" />
=== After the Han Dynasty === The [[:en:Book of Jin|Book of Jin]] discusses the Uneme of [[:en:Emperor Wu of Jin|Emperor Wu of Jin]], with accounts appearing in Volume 3 of the annals of Emperor Wu, Volume 57 of the biography of {{ill|Hu Fen|ja|胡奮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hu Fen|1=Hu Fen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3141784}}, Volume 27 of the upper Five Elements Records, Volume 28 of the middle Five Elements Records, and Volume 31 of the consorts’ records.<ref name="sogabe" />
Regarding the Southern and Northern Dynasties period, the [[:en:History of the Southern Dynasties|History of the Southern Dynasties]] of the [[:en:Liu Song dynasty|Southern Song]] records in Volume 2 that the deposed former emperor [[:en:Liu Ziye|Former Deposed Emperor]], along with the {{ill|Princess of the Mountain Shade|ja|山陰公主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Princess of the Mountain Shade|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and several hundred {{ill|Cai Nu|ja|綵女|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Cai Nu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, followed an assembly of shamans to capture ghosts; further mentions of Uneme appear in Volume 11 in the biography of [[:en:Chen Miaodeng|Later Deposed Empress Chen]].<ref name="sogabe" /> In the [[:en:History of the Northern Dynasties|Book of Northern History]] of the [[:en:Northern Wei|Northern Wei]] (or later Wei), Volume 13 of the consorts’ records notes the existence of the Uneme system, and Volume 10 of the annals of [[:en:Emperor Xuan of Northern Zhou|Emperor Xuan]] includes an account of Uneme.<ref name="sogabe" />
During the [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui Dynasty]] period, Volume 675 of the [[:en:Wenyuan Yinghua|Wenyuan Yinghua]] records that in Emperor [[:en:Emperor Yang of Sui|Yang of Sui]]’s harem there were said to be several hundred to a thousand Uneme.<ref name="sogabe" /> According to [[:en:Zhao Yi|Zhao Yi]], Uneme also existed during the era of the [[:en:Yuan dynasty|Yuan]], as recorded in Volume 30 of the {{ill|Annotated Twenty-Two Histories|ja|二十二史箚記|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Annotated Twenty-Two Histories|1=Notes of the Twenty-Two Histories|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10880068}}.<ref name="sogabe" />
== Uneme in Japan == The earliest mention of Uneme appears in the [[:en:Kojiki|Kojiki]] in the section on [[:en:Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku]], and in the [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] in the section on [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]].<ref name="sogabe">{{Cite journal |type=Japanese book |url=https://doi.org/10.5955/jalha.1951.96 |author={{ill|Sogabe Shizuo|ja|曽我部静雄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sogabe Shizuo|1=Shizuo Sogabe|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q58420170}} |title=The Origins of Attendants, Uneme, and Female Servants |journal=Studies in Legal History |issue=1 |publisher=Legal History Society |date=1951 |pages=96–119}}</ref>
In the 2nd year of the [[:en:Daidō|Daidō]] era (807 AD), the system of Uneme offerings was temporarily abolished, but it was revived during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]]. Thereafter, the position was reserved only for special ceremonies. The head official of the Uneme was known as Uneme-no-Kami.
=== History === Although many aspects of its origins remain unclear, according to the [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]], as early as the [[:en:Asuka period|Asuka Period]], local aristocrats customarily offered their daughters to the [[:en:Imperial House of Japan|Imperial Family]]. Successive generations of Uneme were drawn from the direct families of the emperor as well as from prominent local clans. Moreover, a Taihōkan edict issued in the 17th year of the [[:en:Engi (era)|Engi]] era (917 AD, as indicated by [[:en:917|917]]) by which the governor of Izumo Province (<now rendered as> [[:en:Izumo clan|Izumo Provincial Governor]]) prohibited keeping a concubine under the title {{ill|Jingu Uneme|ja|神宮采女|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingu Uneme|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, except in cases necessary for Shinto ritual, has been cited as evidence that the system emerged during the process in which the imperial family gradually absorbed and integrated local ritual functions. Some scholars have even suggested that Uneme, who were sometimes treated as equivalent to concubines in ritual practices that sometimes involved procreation, may have had their origins in associations with [[:en:Miko|Shrine Maidens]].<ref>『古代豪族』, Aoki Kazuo</ref>
Although their principal duty was to serve in the meal preparations for the emperor, Uneme – who were exclusively selected from among those admired for their beauty from all over the country and who served in close proximity to the emperor – often also fulfilled the role of concubines and bore children. However, as social status at that time placed great importance on the mother’s family background, children born to Uneme from local aristocratic families (the families of {{ill|County Magistrate|ja|郡司|lt=Deputy County Magistrate|lt_ja=郡少領|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/County Magistrate|1=gunji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q4152149}} and above) were generally accorded a lower status compared with those born to central aristocrats or the {{ill|Imperial Family|ja|皇族|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Family|1=Imperial Family of Japan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11581068}}.
The system was formalized by the Imperial Harem Officials Order of the [[:en:Taihō Code|Taibō Ritsuryō]]. Its provisions were as follows: : An edict issued by the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]] allocated quotas to the provinces for recruitment, though the process was nominally termed an “offering.” : The eligibility criteria were: # The candidate had to be between 13 and 30 years old. (In the revived system during [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]]’s reign – after the temporary abolition of the offering system – the age requirement was 16 to 20.) # The candidate had to be a daughter or sister of a family of at least {{ill|County Magistrate|ja|郡司|lt=Deputy County Magistrate|lt_ja=郡少領|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/County Magistrate|1=gunji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q4152149}} Rank. # Their appearance had to be especially refined. : Although the personnel matters of these women were managed by the “Uneme Department” ({{ill|Uneme Department|ja|采女司|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uneme Department|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 采女|1=Uneme|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644506}}) under the {{ill|Imperial Household Ministry|ja|宮内省 (律令制)|lt=Imperial Household Ministry|lt_ja=宮内省|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Ministry|1=Ministry of the Imperial Household (Ritsuryō system)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q125558338}}, in practice they were assigned to two of the Twelve Harem Departments: 6 to the {{ill|Water Department|ja|水司|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water Department|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and 60 to the {{ill|Serving Department|ja|膳司|lt=Kashiwade no Tsukasa|lt_ja=かしわでのつかさ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Serving Department|1=Serving Department|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q97184776}}. Although the official quota was 66, the military defense provisions of the Taibō Ritsuryō stipulated that Uneme should be recruited from one-third of the provinces nationwide; thus, the actual number of Uneme offered greatly exceeded the official quota. It is therefore believed that there were also individuals placed in other departments as substitutes for {{ill|Onamutsu|ja|女嬬|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onamutsu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 女孺|1=nyoju|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10942756}}, or who were employed outside the official quota,<ref>『郡司及び采女制度の研究』, Isokai Masayoshi</ref> or even those attached to imperial princes,<ref>『奈良の都』, Aoki Kazuo</ref> and that some, such as {{ill|Iitakushotaka|ja|飯高諸高|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iitakushotaka|1=Iitakushotaka|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q29410783}}, were later promoted to higher positions (such as {{ill|Dianshi|ja|典侍|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dianshi|1=Naishi-no-suke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10894614}}, {{ill|Chief Attendant|ja|掌侍|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chief Attendant|1=Naishi-no-jō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11498168}}, {{ill|Head of the Serving Department|ja|掌膳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Head of the Serving Department|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, or {{ill|Official Sweeper|ja|典掃|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Official Sweeper|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}), which were also considered outside the official Uneme quota. In this period when Uneme were integrated into the [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō System]], their role as wives or concubines of the emperor diminished, and they increasingly came to be regarded as lower-Ranking officials within the imperial harem. Many of them likely became {{ill|Maid|ja|女孺|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maid|1=nyoju|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10942756}}.<ref>{{Cite book |author={{ill|Keiji Nagahara|ja|永原慶二|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Keiji Nagahara|1=Keiji Nagahara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11549910}} |title=Iwanami Dictionary of Japanese History |publisher=Iwanami Shoten |date=1999}}</ref>
Reforms under [[:en:Emperor Heizei|Emperor Heizei]] abolished the system of Uneme offerings, and accordingly the Uneme Department was also dissolved, being merged with the Department of Sewing ({{ill|Department of Sewing|ja|縫部司|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Department of Sewing|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 縫殿寮|1=Department of Sewing|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11608161}}) in the {{ill|Sewing Hall|ja|縫殿寮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sewing Hall|1=Sewing Hall|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11608161}} of the [[:en:Ministry of the Treasury|Finance Ministry]]. However, the offering system and the Uneme Department were revived during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]]. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|Engishiki|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the official quota for Uneme was reduced to 41 in the {{ill|Serving Department|ja|膳司|lt=Kashiwade no Tsukasa|lt_ja=かしわでのつかさ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Serving Department|1=Serving Department|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q97184776}} and 6 in the {{ill|Cleaning Department|ja|掃司|lt=Kanomori no Tsukasa|lt_ja=かにもりのつかさ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Cleaning Department|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Thereafter, Uneme were increasingly selected from the daughters of central nobles, and the role became increasingly ceremonial. From the [[:en:Edo period|Edo Period]] onward, Uneme were chosen from among the court ladies only at the time of the [[:en:Enthronement of the Japanese emperor|Enthronement Ceremony]] for the emperor; at that time, instead of wearing the full formal attire of the court ladies ([[:en:Jūnihitoe|Junihitoe]]), they donned a special, short {{ill|Uneme Costume|ja|采女装束|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uneme Costume|1=uneme shōzoku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644509}}.
=== Etymology === Several theories have been proposed regarding the origin of the word “uneme.” These include [[:en:Motoori Norinaga|Motoori Norinaga]]’s “Unagee” theory (嬰部（うなげえ）), [[:en:Ogyū Sorai|Ogyū Sorai]]’s “Unawime” theory (項意（うなゐめ）), [[:en:Kamo no Mabuchi|Kamo no Maifuchi]]’s “Unome” theory (氏之女（うのめ）), and {{ill|Tsuboi Yoshitomo|ja|壺井義知|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuboi Yoshitomo|1=Tsuboi Yoshichika|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6536790}}’s “Uneme” theory (畝女（うねめ）).
=== Uneme as Objects of Admiration === Uneme were reputed to be largely drawn from local aristocratic families, celebrated for their exquisite beauty and high cultural accomplishments. Owing to the fact that only the [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]] was permitted personal contact with them, they have long been objects of male admiration. In earlier times, the [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]]’s section on [[:en:Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku]] describes the Uneme as having “exceptionally beautiful features and a refined appearance,” while the {{ill|Hyakuryō Kun'yōshū|ja|百寮訓要集|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hyakuryō Kun'yōshū|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} states that “the Uneme are women selected from among the most beautiful in the land to serve the Son of Heaven.” The {{ill|Kokinshū|ja|古今集|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokinshū|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 古今和歌集|1=Kokin Wakashū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1047167}} also contains many gentle allusions in its poetry, and the {{ill|Wakan Kanjō Hisho|ja|和漢官職秘抄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakan Kanjō Hisho|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} records that “in some accounts, either through the fame of a beauty or the renown of her poetry – or by virtue of a refined aptitude in playing the koto and the se – a woman would be presented by local officials.” Furthermore, the [[:en:Man'yōshū|Man'yōshū]] includes the famous poem celebrating how [[:en:Fujiwara no Kamatari|Fujiwara no Kamatari]] rejoiced at receiving the Uneme Yasumi from [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]]: “われはもや安見児得たり 皆人の得難にすとふ安見児得たり” In addition, a poem by [[:en:Prince Shiki|Prince Shiki]]—“The Uneme’s sleeves flutter, like the Asuka breeze, playfully blowing far from the capital”—reveals the deep admiration that men felt for these beautiful Uneme.
== Legendary Uneme == === The Legend of Sarusawa Pond / Yama no I Legend === : In the [[:en:Yamato Monogatari|Yamato Monogatari]], there is a legend concerning the “Emperor of Nara” (displayed as [[:en:Tachibana no Moroe|Katsuragi-ō]]) and an Uneme known as Haruhime. : It is noteworthy that interpretations of the related Man'yōshū poems differ between the two versions—for instance, whether the poem “Even the shadows of Mount Azumi can be seen in the shallow heart of the mountain well” conveys a sentiment of passionate love or sincere devotion, and whether the poem “My sister’s disheveled hair, I see it sorrowfully in the jeweled waters of Sarusawa Pond” evokes the image of hair floating like seaweed from a drowned body or recalls the hair as it was in life. : On the basis of this legend, [[:en:Nara (city)|Nara City]] and [[:en:Kōriyama|Koriyama City]] have established a sister cities relationship. * Sarusawa Pond *: According to both the account in the Yamato Monogatari and local tradition in Nara City, a certain Uneme—who had fallen out of favor with the “Emperor of Nara” (during the [[:en:Nara period|Nara Period]], referred to as Saru Tennō)—committed suicide by leaping into Sarusawa Pond. This event served as the motif for the {{ill|Uneme (Noh)|ja|采女 (謡曲)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uneme (Noh)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. : As a memorial to her spirit, an annual festival – the {{ill|Uneme Festival|ja|采女祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uneme Festival|1=Uneme Matsuri|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644507}} – is held during the time of the {{ill|Mid-Autumn Moon|ja|中秋の名月|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mid-Autumn Moon|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 月見|1=tsukimi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1050292}} at the {{ill|Uneme Shrine|ja|采女神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uneme Shrine|1=Uneme Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q22118013}}, located along the banks of {{ill|Sarusawa Pond|ja|猿沢池|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarusawa Pond|1=Sarusawa Pond|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11572131}} in Nara. * The Yama no I Legend *: In a legend from Koriyama City, a prelude and sequel exist: It is said that when the Katsuragi-ō (who had come on an inspection tour to Mutsu Province) first laid eyes on Haruhime, the daughter of the head of the Azumi village, he brought her back to the capital. However, missing her betrothed, Haruhime feigned an accidental plunge into Sarusawa Pond in order to return home. Later, after her lover cast himself into the clear waters of a mountain well, Haruhime followed him in a final act of suicide. In connection with this legend, the local {{ill|Uneme Shrine (Koriyama)|ja|采女神社 (郡山市)|lt=Uneme Shrine|lt_ja=采女神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uneme Shrine (Koriyama)|1=Uneme Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q48757571}} exists, as does a local festival – the {{ill|Koriyama Uneme Festival|ja|郡山うねめまつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koriyama Uneme Festival|1=Kōriyama Uneme Festival|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11643131}} – established at the time of the merger of Koriyama City and {{ill|Azumi District|ja|安積郡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Azumi District|1=Asaka district|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11451165}}. There is also a tourism ambassador known as “Miss Uneme” who is selected through a {{ill|Miss Contest|ja|ミスコンテスト|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miss Contest|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ミス・コンテスト|1=beauty contest|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2658935}}. === Kojiki Legend === : During the reign of [[:en:Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku]], it is recorded in the [[:en:Kojiki|Kojiki]] that “the threefold Uneme of {{ill|Ise Province|ja|伊勢の国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Province|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 伊勢国|1=Ise Province|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q864166}},” while serving at a banquet for the emperor, unwittingly poured wine into a ceremonial cup containing leaves. This act incurred the emperor’s wrath and nearly led to her execution; however, she spontaneously composed a poem extolling the emperor and praying for prosperity, and the excellence of her verse so impressed the emperor that her life was spared. Furthermore, a place named “Uneme” exists in both [[:en:Mie Prefecture|Mie Prefecture]] and [[:en:Yokkaichi|Yokkaichi City]].
